title: 价格、竞争与市场的运转
topic: How supply, demand, and competition shape a market economy

sentences.en: Today I want to walk you through one of the most powerful ideas in economics: how the price of any commodity, from a barrel of oil to a bag of coffee, is actually decided.
sentences.zh: 今天我想带大家理清经济学里最有威力的一个观念：任何一样商品的价格——不管是一桶石油还是一袋咖啡——究竟是怎么被决定的。

sentences.en: The short answer is the tug-of-war between supply and demand, and once you really understand that push and pull, a lot of the business world suddenly makes sense.
sentences.zh: 简短的答案，就是供给与需求之间的一场拔河；而一旦你真正理解了这一推一拉，商业世界里的许多现象一下子就说得通了。

sentences.en: Supply is simply how much of a good producers are willing to bring to market, while demand is how much buyers actually want to purchase at a given price.
sentences.zh: 供给，无非就是生产者愿意拿到市场上出售的货量；而需求，则是买家在某个价格下真正想购买的数量。

sentences.en: When supply outruns demand, you get a surplus, and sellers sitting on unsold merchandise are forced to cut prices to clear their shelves.
sentences.zh: 当供给超过需求时，就会出现过剩，那些手里压着卖不掉商品的卖家，只好降价来清空货架。

sentences.en: When demand outruns supply, you get the opposite—a shortage or deficit—and prices climb because buyers compete for whatever is available.
sentences.zh: 而当需求超过供给时，情况正好相反——出现短缺或供不应求——价格随之攀升，因为买家在争抢仅有的货源。

sentences.en: Now, if too much money is chasing too few goods across the whole economy, prices rise everywhere at once, and that broad, general increase is what we call inflation.
sentences.zh: 如果放到整个经济来看，是太多的钱在追逐太少的商品，那么各处物价便同时上涨，这种普遍而全面的物价上升，就是我们所说的通货膨胀。

sentences.en: Prices matter because they act as signals: a high price is an incentive that tells an entrepreneur, ‘There is money to be made here—go build something.’
sentences.zh: 价格之所以重要，是因为它充当着信号：高价就是一种激励，它在告诉创业者「这里有钱可赚——去干一番事业吧」。

sentences.en: So a founder launches a new venture, borrows money, and uses that finance to buy assets like machines and a building where the firm can manufacture goods to sell at retail for more than they cost.
sentences.zh: 于是创业者开办一个新的（有风险的）项目，借来钱，用这笔资金购置机器和厂房这类资产，好让公司在里面成批制造产品，再以高于成本的零售价卖出去。

sentences.en: Every sale is a transaction, and the total money flowing in from all those sales is the firm's revenue.
sentences.zh: 每一笔买卖都是一次交易，而所有这些销售所流入的钱的总额，就是这家公司的营收。

sentences.en: But revenue is not profit; the company still has to cover its expenditure—wages, rent, materials—all the costs written into its annual budget.
sentences.zh: 但营收并不等于利润；公司还得覆盖它的各项支出——工资、租金、原材料——所有写进年度预算里的成本。

sentences.en: If revenue comfortably exceeds expenditure, the firm earns a profit, and it may pay part of that back to its shareholders as a dividend.
sentences.zh: 如果营收从容地超过支出，公司就赚到了利润，并且可能把其中一部分作为股息回馈给股东。

sentences.en: To keep costs down and stay competitive, businesses obsess over productivity—getting more output from every worker, every machine, every hour.
sentences.zh: 为了压低成本、保持竞争力，企业极为看重生产率——让每个工人、每台机器、每小时都产出更多。

sentences.en: One way to protect an edge is a patent, a legal right that lets an inventor stop rivals from copying a new design for a fixed number of years.
sentences.zh: 保护自身优势的一种办法是专利，这是一种法律权利，能让发明人在若干年内阻止对手仿造某项新设计。

sentences.en: But when a single company controls a market so completely that no rival can enter, we call that a monopoly, and prices tend to rise because buyers have nowhere else to go.
sentences.zh: 但当一家公司把某个市场牢牢掌控到没有对手能够进入时，我们就称之为垄断；此时价格往往上涨，因为买家别无去处。

sentences.en: This is why competition sits at the heart of healthy commerce: rival firms negotiate, undercut, and innovate, and the customer walks away paying less.
sentences.zh: 这正是为什么竞争处于健康商业的核心：彼此竞争的公司相互磋商、压价、创新，而顾客最终以更低的价钱买单。

sentences.en: Governments step in too—sometimes with a subsidy that lowers a producer's costs, sometimes with a tariff that taxes imported goods to shield domestic enterprise.
sentences.zh: 政府也会介入——有时用补贴来降低生产者的成本，有时用关税对进口商品征税，以保护本国企业。

sentences.en: These tools can protect jobs, but they also distort prices, so economists argue endlessly about whether a given tariff helps or harms in the long run.
sentences.zh: 这些手段可以保护就业，但也会扭曲价格，所以经济学家们没完没了地争论：某项关税从长远看究竟是有益还是有害。

sentences.en: Zoom out, and all of these transactions rise and fall together in what we call the business cycle.
sentences.zh: 把镜头拉远，所有这些交易会一同起伏，构成我们所说的经济周期。

sentences.en: In the good years, spending is high, factories run flat out, and the whole country enjoys prosperity; when a nation sells more abroad than it buys, it even runs a trade surplus.
sentences.zh: 在景气的年头，消费旺盛，工厂开足马力，整个国家享受着繁荣；当一国对外卖出的多于买入的，它甚至会出现贸易顺差。

sentences.en: But in the down years, demand collapses, unemployment climbs, and the economy slides into a recession, with more money flowing out than in—a deficit.
sentences.zh: 但在萧条的年头，需求崩塌，失业上升，经济滑入衰退，流出的钱多于流入的——出现赤字。

sentences.en: So the next time you see a price change on a shelf, remember it is not random: it is supply, demand, incentives, and policy—the whole machinery of the market—quietly at work.
sentences.zh: 所以，下次你看到货架上价格变动时，记住那并非随机：那是供给、需求、激励与政策——整台市场的机器——在悄然运转。
